questions.prompt: Prove the Basic Proportionality Theorem: a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides in the same ratio.

answerKey.modelAnswer: In ΔABC let D lie on AB and E on AC with DE ∥ BC. Areas of ΔADE and ΔDBE have the same altitude to AB, so their ratio is AD:DB. Areas of ΔADE and ΔDEC have the same altitude to AC, so their ratio is AE:EC. Triangles DBE and DEC have equal bases DE and equal altitudes because BC ∥ DE, so their areas are equal. Hence AD/DB = AE/EC.

markingScheme.criterion: Set up the two area ratios (2 marks).
Show areas of ΔDBE and ΔDEC are equal (1 mark).

answerKey.modelAnswer: For similar ΔABC and ΔPQR, corresponding altitudes are in the same ratio as corresponding sides. Using area = ½×base×height, the area ratio is the product of the base ratio and altitude ratio, hence the square of the side ratio.

markingScheme.criterion: State corresponding sides and altitudes are proportional (1 mark).
Write the ratio of areas using base and altitude (2 marks).
Conclude the area ratio is the square of the side ratio (2 marks).
